evals.prompt: We just published a 2500-word original study on our blog at https://forecastly.io/blog/2026-demand-planning-benchmark with survey data from 400 supply chain managers. It got almost no traffic. We sell demand planning software to mid-market manufacturers. Give me a plan to repurpose this into a week or two of social content so it actually gets seen and helps us long term.
evals.expected_output: A repurposing pipeline that starts from the pillar study and atomizes it into native formats per platform (a query-titled YouTube video walking through the headline findings with a transcript and an on-site embed on the article; LinkedIn text and document posts stating individual data points as standalone insights, not link teasers; X threads from the findings; short vertical clips of the most surprising stats for Shorts/Reels if the audience fits), with an explicit rule against posting the same link everywhere and a one-to-two-week staggered cadence. Prioritizes platforms by SEO and GEO return for a B2B manufacturing audience (YouTube first, LinkedIn high, Reddit and relevant communities under the 95/5 rule, X by fit), not by reach. States the indirect value honestly (branded search, AI citation surfaces, entity reinforcement; nofollow social links pass no PageRank), routes mention placement and listicle inclusion to seo-backlinks, applies geo-visibility citability rules to the video description and posts, and hands measurement to geo-tracking (branded search in GSC, AI and social referrals in GA4) while stating that likes and follower counts are not the outcome. Closes the loop by feeding overperforming angles back to seo-keyword-research. Labels the YouTube near 15% citation figure and cadence numbers as field heuristics and cites measured claims (Semrush most cited domains, Profound Perplexity overweighting, Ahrefs 0.664 vs 0.218) with URLs.

evals.prompt: When people ask ChatGPT or Perplexity for the best tool in our category, we never come up. Someone told me being active on Reddit and YouTube would fix that. Is that true, and if so how do I actually do it? We're a project management SaaS.
evals.expected_output: Confirms the premise with the correct mechanism: YouTube, Reddit, and LinkedIn are among the most cited domains in AI answers and Perplexity overweights YouTube and user-generated content, so building genuine presence there makes the brand citable (with the geo-visibility pointer for the full surface list and citability rules, and the note that geo-tracking measures whether it works). For YouTube, prescribes query-titled videos with rich descriptions, accurate transcripts (engines read the text, not the video), and on-site embeds. For Reddit and communities, prescribes genuine participation under the strict 95/5 rule with an explicit no-astroturfing warning, and gives the honest volatility caveat that Reddit's ChatGPT citation share moved from roughly 60% to roughly 10% in about a month (Semrush), so participate cleanly but never bet everything on it. Routes the deliberate get-the-brand-mentioned-in-threads program and listicle inclusion to seo-backlinks, recommends a consistent LinkedIn company page with the canonical one-line description for B2B entity corroboration, and warns against being thin on every platform. Cites measured claims (Semrush, Profound) with URLs and labels the YouTube near 15% figure as a field heuristic.

evals.prompt: Straight question: does posting on social media actually help my Google SEO? My agency keeps telling me to post daily on LinkedIn and Instagram and that the likes and shares will boost our rankings. I run a regional accounting firm.
evals.expected_output: An honest answer that social signals (likes, shares, follower counts) are NOT a direct Google ranking factor, a position Google has stated publicly and repeatedly, and that the 'shares boost rankings' claim is a myth to be corrected, while explaining that social does help SEO and GEO indirectly through three mechanisms: branded search (people who see the brand later search it by name, and branded search and brand mentions correlate with rankings and AI visibility, Ahrefs 0.664 vs 0.218), presence on the third-party surfaces AI engines cite, and reinforcement of the brand entity through consistent co-occurrence. Notes that social links are nofollow and pass no PageRank (pointer to seo-backlinks). Pushes back on the daily-everywhere advice as dilution and on reporting likes as an outcome, recommends focusing on the two or three platforms matched to the audience (for a regional accounting firm, likely LinkedIn and a local-relevant channel over Instagram, with seo-local for local profile consistency), and frames the real outcome as branded search, referral traffic, conversions, and AI citations measured in geo-tracking. Separates measured claims (Ahrefs, with URL) from field heuristics.
